title: How a Car Engine Works in 60 Seconds 🚗🔥 #shorts
description:
Every car engine runs the same four-stroke dance. The piston sucks in air and fuel, squeezes it, a spark makes it explode, and the piston pushes the burnt gas out, while the crankshaft turns all that up-and-down motion into spin for your wheels. Suck, squeeze, bang, blow. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#carengine #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: The Engine
steps.text: At highway speed, a four-cylinder engine fires about *100 sparks* every second.

steps.label: Intake
steps.text: Stroke one: *intake*. The piston slides down and sucks in air mixed with a mist of fuel.

steps.label: Compression
steps.text: Stroke two: *compression*. The piston rises and squeezes that mix into about a tenth of the space.

steps.label: Power
steps.text: Stroke three: *power*. A spark ignites the mix, and the blast shoves the piston down hard.

steps.label: Exhaust
steps.text: Stroke four: *exhaust*. The piston rises again and pushes the burnt gas out.

steps.label: Crankshaft
steps.text: A rod turns all that up-and-down motion into spin on the *crankshaft*, which drives your wheels.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Suck, squeeze, *bang*, blow. Follow Inside 60 for more.
